title: The AMQP model
summary: Connections, channels, exchanges, bindings, queues and routing keys: how a message finds its queue in RabbitMQ, declared with the RabbitMQ.Client 7 async API.

steps.title: Publishers never write to queues
body: RabbitMQ speaks **AMQP 0-9-1**. A publisher sends a message to an **exchange** with a **routing key**. The
exchange looks at its **bindings** and copies the message into every queue whose binding matches. Consumers
read from **queues**.
```text
orders-api ══ TCP connection (one per process) ════════════════╗  RabbitMQ, vhost "/"
├─ channel 1: publishes                                       ║
└─ channel 2: consumes                                        ║
publish(exchange: "orders", routingKey: "order.eu.created")     ║
v                                                        ║
[ exchange "orders" (topic) ] ─ binding "order.*.created" ─> [ queue "billing" ] ──> billing consumer
└ binding "order.#" ─────────> [ queue "audit" ]   ──> audit consumer
- A **connection** is a real TCP (+TLS) connection: expensive, long-lived, one per process.
- A **channel** is a lightweight session multiplexed inside it. Use one per concurrent publisher or consumer;
do not publish from many threads on one channel at once.
- A **vhost** is a namespace with its own exchanges, queues and permissions.
Because publishers only know the exchange, you can add a queue (a new subscriber) without touching them.

steps.prompt: Match each AMQP term to what it is.
pairs: Receives publishes and routes copies to queues by its type and bindings
A rule "queue Q wants messages from exchange X whose key matches K"
A dot-separated label the publisher puts on each message
Stores messages in order until a consumer acknowledges them
A lightweight session inside one TCP connection
steps.explain: Exchanges route, queues store. A message that matches no binding is not stored anywhere: more on that next lesson.

steps.title: Declaring topology with RabbitMQ.Client 7
body: RabbitMQ.Client 7 is **async-only**. Declarations are idempotent: declaring something that already exists with
the same settings is a no-op, so every service declares what it needs at startup.
```csharp
var factory = new ConnectionFactory { HostName = "localhost", ClientProvidedName = "orders-api" };
await using var connection = await factory.CreateConnectionAsync();
await using var channel = await connection.CreateChannelAsync();
await channel.ExchangeDeclareAsync("orders", ExchangeType.Topic, durable: true);
await channel.QueueDeclareAsync("billing", durable: true, exclusive: false, autoDelete: false,
arguments: new Dictionary<string, object?> { ["x-queue-type"] = "quorum" });
await channel.QueueBindAsync("billing", "orders", "order.*.created");
- `durable: true` means the **exchange or queue definition** survives a broker restart. The **messages** survive
only if they are persistent too (`Persistent = true`), or the queue is a quorum queue.
- Declaring an existing queue with **different** arguments fails with `PRECONDITION_FAILED` and closes the
channel. That is why settings you want to change later belong in **policies** (lesson 4).
> **Older code:** RabbitMQ.Client 6.x was synchronous: `factory.CreateConnection()`, `connection.CreateModel()`
> (an `IModel`), `channel.QueueDeclare(...)`, `EventingBasicConsumer` with `Received`. You will still find it;
> write new code against 7.x.

steps.prompt: Arrange the startup code of a service that declares its topology.
lines: var factory = new ConnectionFactory { HostName = "localhost", ClientProvidedName = "billing" };
await using var connection = await factory.CreateConnectionAsync();
await using var channel = await connection.CreateChannelAsync();
await channel.QueueDeclareAsync("billing", durable: true, exclusive: false, autoDelete: false);
also: var factory = new ConnectionFactory { HostName = "localhost", ClientProvidedName = "billing" };
await using var connection = await factory.CreateConnectionAsync();
await using var channel = await connection.CreateChannelAsync();
await channel.QueueDeclareAsync("billing", durable: true, exclusive: false, autoDelete: false);
steps.explain: Connection, then channel, then declarations. The exchange and the queue can be declared in either order, but both must exist before the binding that joins them.

steps.prompt: A script publishes with an **empty exchange name**. Where does the message go?
code: basicProperties: new BasicProperties { Persistent = true }, body: body);
options: Straight into the queue named `billing`: the default exchange binds every queue by its own name
To every queue, like a fanout exchange
Nowhere: an empty exchange name is an error
steps.explain: The default exchange (`""`) is a direct exchange that every queue is automatically bound to with its own name. Handy for scripts and work queues; for events, publish to a named exchange so subscribers can bind.

steps.title: Exchange types
body: | Type | Routes to the queues whose binding... | Typical use |
| **direct** | key **equals** the routing key | commands to a named worker queue |
| **topic** | pattern matches the key: words split by `.`, `*` = **exactly one** word, `#` = **zero or more** words | events by category: `order.eu.created` |
| **fanout** | (all bound queues; the key is ignored) | broadcast to every subscriber |
| **headers** | arguments match the message **headers** (`x-match: all` or `any`) | routing on several attributes |
```text
routing key  order.eu.created
order.*.created   ✓   (* = eu)
order.#           ✓   (# = eu.created)
#.created         ✓
order.*           ✗   (* is exactly one word, two are left)
A topic binding without wildcards behaves like direct; a binding of `#` behaves like fanout.
> **See it:** open **Labs → Messaging builder → RabbitMQ** and play *First binding*, *The wildcard that never
> matches* and *Everyone gets a copy*.

steps.prompt: A message is published with routing key `order.eu.created` to a topic exchange. Which binding keys match it?
steps.explain: `*` must consume exactly one word and `#` any number, including zero. Count the words on both sides.

steps.title: Direct, fanout and the default exchange
prompt: Write `List<string> Route(string exchange, string type, string routingKey, (string Queue, string Key)[] bindings, string[] queues)`
returning the queues that receive the message:
- `exchange == ""` (the default exchange): `[routingKey]` if a queue with that name exists in `queues`, else
- `"direct"`: the queues whose binding key **equals** the routing key (case-sensitive).
- `"fanout"`: every bound queue, whatever the key.
Each queue appears **once** (a queue bound twice gets one copy), in the order of its first binding.
starter: List<string> Route(string exchange, string type, string routingKey, (string Queue, string Key)[] bindings, string[] queues)
solution: List<string> Route(string exchange, string type, string routingKey, (string Queue, string Key)[] bindings, string[] queues)
return queues.Contains(routingKey) ? new List<string> { routingKey } : new List<string>();
_ => throw new ArgumentException($"unsupported exchange type '{type}'", nameof(type)),
hints: `bindings.Where(b => b.Key == routingKey).Select(b => b.Queue).Distinct().ToList()` keeps first-binding order.
template: Dojo.Eq("direct: both bound queues get order.created", new List<string> { "billing", "audit" }, Route("orders", "direct", "order.created", dojoB, dojoQ));
Dojo.Eq("direct: refunds only", new List<string> { "refunds" }, Route("orders", "direct", "order.refunded", dojoB, dojoQ));
Dojo.Eq("direct: no binding, no queue", new List<string>(), Route("orders", "direct", "order.shipped", dojoB, dojoQ));
Dojo.Eq("direct keys are case-sensitive", new List<string>(), Route("orders", "direct", "Order.Created", dojoB, dojoQ));
Dojo.Eq("fanout ignores the key", new List<string> { "billing", "audit", "refunds" }, Route("broadcast", "fanout", "anything", dojoB, dojoQ));
Dojo.Eq("default exchange routes by queue name", new List<string> { "refunds" }, Route("", "direct", "refunds", dojoB, dojoQ));
Dojo.Eq("default exchange, unknown queue", new List<string>(), Route("", "direct", "nope", dojoB, dojoQ));
Dojo.Throws<ArgumentException>("unknown exchange type", () => Route("orders", "x-random", "k", dojoB, dojoQ));
